response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS order_avg FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), overall AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS overall_avg FROM orderexecutions), above_overall AS (SELECT p.order_avg, p.order_avg - o.overall_avg AS excess_overall FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.order_avg > o.overall_avg), group_avg AS (SELECT AVG(order_avg) AS second_avg FROM above_overall) SELECT AVG(a.order_avg) AS average_order_avg, AVG(a.excess_overall) AS average_excess_overall, AVG(a.order_avg - g.second_avg) AS average_excess_second FROM above_overall a CROSS JOIN group_avg g WHERE a.order_avg > g.second_avg;

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is taken across executions with non-null remaincount, so orders with more executions have more weight in that average.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the average of the per-order averages, giving each order equal weight.
